items.title: Herbie Hancock interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 18, 1995
items.q: Chick and I — I should say about when we first got together to do the first tour... we wound up actually doing two tours. One was in ‘76 and I think the other one was in 1978.

ctx.x: Talk to us about the, you know, the two of you like spurring each other on, learning from each other, just like the virtuosity of the language, you know.

We — Chick and I — I should say about when we first got together to do the first tour, you know, when we first got together to rehearse, neither one of us had done anything quite like that before. He had done some duets I guess with his, well his then-girlfriend, now wife, Gayle Moran, who was working in his band and she’s also a singer. But there was sort of a different story because she hadn’t had the same kinds of experiences. She wasn’t like a heavyweight piano player per se, that wasn’t what she was about.…

thought.” It just happens that Chick and I just really fit each other. Somehow it just works. It’s amazing, you know, really amazing. I’ve had the great fortune also to play five concerts opposite Oscar Peterson but we played a couple of things together. So I mean that was a great opportunity for me. He’s one of the people that was a major influence on me when I was coming up. That’s a little more difficult, playing with Oscar. Maybe because he has been his own man for so long that he’s used to doing certain…
